text: The Web activity calls a custom REST endpoint from inside a pipeline — GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE — and can pass datasets and linked services along as part of the request itself. Real uses include triggering an external system once a load finishes, or posting a status update straight to a Teams or Slack webhook.

Three more small activities, each doing exactly one real thing. Wait pauses the pipeline for a specified number of seconds before continuing on — useful for waiting out a known external delay, or spacing out retries deliberately. Fail deliberately fails the pipeline with a custom error message and error code you actually define yourself. And Set Variable writes a value into a pipeline variable that's already been defined, so a later activity can read it back.

Fail genuinely sounds backwards until you actually see it used. Pair it with an If Condition checking something that should be true before continuing — a row count above zero, a file that actually exists — and branch to Fail with a clear, custom message the moment it isn't. A pipeline that stops loudly with an explanation beats one that quietly succeeds on bad data every single time.

None of these four activities move or transform data on their own. They're the small, deliberate pieces that make a pipeline's control flow actually correct: reach outside the pipeline, pause on purpose, stop loudly when something's genuinely wrong, and track state as the pipeline runs. Next: putting every activity from this entire chapter together into one real, working, end-to-end pipeline.
